title: Speculative decoding with a self-drafting head
summary: We attach a lightweight drafting head to the base model so a single forward pass proposes several tokens, which the base model then verifies in parallel. On a 70B model the method reaches 2.4x wall-clock speedup at batch size 1 with identical output distributions. Gains fall to 1.3x at batch size 32 because verification stops being the bottleneck.
whats_new: A drafting head trained on the base model's own hidden states, so no second model has to be served.
what_it_replaces: Two-model speculative decoding, which needs a separate draft model in memory.
caveat: Gains fall to 1.3x at batch size 32, so this is a latency win, not a throughput win.
builder_takeaway: Worth it if you serve interactive single-stream traffic; skip it if you batch aggressively.
grounded_claims: The drafting head is trained on the base model's hidden states.
Output distributions are identical to the base model.
2.4x wall-clock speedup at batch size 1 on a 70B model.
unverified_claims: It will make every inference stack faster.

title: A benchmark for long-horizon agent memory
summary: The benchmark runs agents over 200-turn sessions and measures whether facts stated early are still used correctly late. Retrieval-augmented memory scores 61% while a full-context baseline scores 74%, but the full-context baseline costs 9x more per session. Every method degrades sharply after turn 120.
whats_new: A benchmark that measures memory over 200-turn sessions rather than single retrieval hops.
what_it_replaces: Single-hop retrieval benchmarks that never test whether an agent keeps a fact.
caveat: Every method degrades sharply after turn 120, so no approach is solved.
builder_takeaway: If your sessions are short, retrieval memory is fine; the gap only opens up late.
grounded_claims: Full-context baseline scores 74% at 9x the cost per session.

title: 4-bit quantization regressions on reasoning tasks
summary: The repository evaluates 4-bit weight-only quantization across eight models. Perplexity moves less than 1%, but chain-of-thought accuracy drops 6 points on average, concentrated in multi-step arithmetic. Activation-aware methods recover about half of the loss.
whats_new: Perplexity-neutral quantization still costs 6 points of chain-of-thought accuracy.
what_it_replaces: Perplexity as the default acceptance test for a quantized model.
caveat: Activation-aware methods recover about half the loss, so the gap is narrowable.
builder_takeaway: Stop shipping a quantized model on a perplexity check; run your reasoning evals.
grounded_claims: Eight models were evaluated with 4-bit weight-only quantization.
Chain-of-thought accuracy drops 6 points on average.
Activation-aware methods recover about half of the loss.
